incident.failedStep: Read back Portal V2 DOM, standalone routing and CSRD assets
incident.symptom: The overview rendered only a fallback sentence when profile maturity was missing, so the adoption curve and organisation-state surfaces disappeared.
incident.rootCause: Semantic parity was conditional on populated customer profile data. Empty-state rendering collapsed multiple protected legacy surfaces into one text card.

truthRule.principle: Missing customer data may change values and confidence, but must not remove protected decision surfaces.
truthRule.unknownState: Render the full surface with explicit unknown/not-filled labels; never synthesize a maturity stage, blocker or CMMI score.
truthRule.customerTruth: Only explicit customer input or eligible evidence may select a current adoption stage or organisation status.

prevention: Protected legacy surfaces must have populated, partial and empty-state production readback coverage.
Do not use empty-state fallbacks that collapse required models, charts, navigation or management surfaces.
A parity test must assert structural presence independently from whether business data exists.
Production DOM readback is authoritative for whether a surface is actually delivered.
Canonical delivery metadata fields such as Supersedes must use the controller-approved value format; recovery context belongs in prose, not inside the metadata value.

Any chat, agent or workflow touching Portal V2 parity must load brain/skills/portal-v2-parity-empty-state-v1.json before execution and must reuse this fingerprint instead of rediscovering the incident.

skillWriteback.rule: The incident learning is not terminal until it is discoverable and executable through the canonical Powerhouse skill and agent-learning surfaces.

admissionRecovery.correction: Supersedes normalized to none; PR #2004 recovery context retained in prose

definitionOfDone: exact-head tests/gates -> protected merge -> main readback -> exact production deploy -> learning/documentation writeback -> canonical skill promotion and agent discovery
